name: Supplementary Nutrition Programme- Bihar
summary: The programme aims to enhance the nutritional level of normal/malnourished/severely malnourished children aged 6 months to 6 years, as well as pregnant women and lactating mothers, through Anganwadi centers. This programme is centrally sponsored with a funding ratio of 50:50.

sections.overview: The &quot;Supplementary Nutrition Programme&quot; is implemented by the Social Welfare Department, Government of Bihar, across all districts of the state under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme (Mission Mode). The programme aims to enhance the nutritional level of normal/malnourished/severely malnourished children aged 6 months to 6 years, as well as pregnant women and lactating mothers, through Anganwadi centers. The nutritional standards in the state are set in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, New Delhi. This programme is centrally sponsored with a funding ratio of 50:50 between the Central and State governments.
sections.eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a resident of Bihar.
   1. All children aged 6 months to 6 years, as well as pregnant women and lactating mothers enrolled in Anganwadi centers across the state, are eligible to receive benefits under the programme.
sections.benefits:
Under this scheme, hot cooked meals and Take-Home Rations (THR) are provided to children aged 6 months to 3 years, as well as pregnant women and lactating mothers enrolled at Anganwadi centers.

  - **Hot Cooked Meals:** Children attending Anganwadi centers for pre-school education, aged 3 to 6 years, receive Khichdi three days a week, Pulao one day, Rasiyav one day, and Semolina pudding one day. Hot cooked food is provided uniformly across Anganwadi centers in all districts for a total of 25 days each month. On Wednesdays and Fridays, children who consume eggs receive a boiled egg for breakfast, while non-egg eaters are given sprouted gram and jaggery.  - **Take-Home Rations (THR):** Dry rations are distributed once a month, covering 25 days, to pregnant women, lactating mothers, and normal, malnourished, and severely malnourished children aged 6 months to 3 years. Pregnant and lactating mothers who consume eggs are provided with a boiled egg every Wednesday and Friday (seven times a month) at the Anganwadi center, while non-egg eaters receive soybean. Children aged 6 months to 3 years who consume eggs are also given a boiled egg on Wednesdays and Fridays, with soybean provided for non-egg eaters.  - **Morning Snacks:** If the district-level price fixation committee increases the price of any item, the additional cost is covered by the morning snack budget. Any savings from other items are used to provide sprouted gram-jaggery, jaggery-chura, or similar items for breakfast.
**Note:** Every Wednesday, 18 grams of milk powder (mixed in 150 ml of warm water) is provided to each child aged 3 to 6 years at 25 Anganwadi centers in 5 districts (Gaya, Saran, Siwan, Gopalganj, and Vaishali) under a pilot project, which has since been expanded across the state.

name: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Digital Planetarium/Space And Astronomy Education Centre (Category 1, Category 2 And Category 3)
summary: The scheme component aims to create awareness about the sky, space and celestial phenomena and to eradicate related superstitions. Capital cost and corpus fund assistance under three categories is provided to State/Union Territory Governments and their Societies.

sections.overview: The component "Digital Planetarium/Space and Astronomy Education Centre" under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to create awareness about the sky, space and celestial phenomena, to integrate astronomy education with physical, mathematical and weather science, and to help eradicate superstitions associated with celestial bodies and phenomena. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and corpus fund is provided under three categories to State Governments, Union Territories, and the Societies or Authorities promoted by the State or Union Territory Governments. The Digital Planetarium or Space and Astronomy Education Centre is being added as a new component in the scheme to enhance the Science Centre experience for students and the general public, and it may be co-located in the existing science centres or could be set up in any institution of non-formal learning engaged in science communication activities. The principal objective is twofold, namely to provide a fundamental concept about the celestial bodies, cosmic events and space science, and to alleviate superstitions and misconceptions about planets, stars, eclipses and so forth. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To introduce the sky to the students and the general public, with its innumerable celestial objects and their movement, and thus to create an awareness about astronomy. - To develop an understanding about the sky and the space and about the celestial phenomena. - To integrate the astronomical knowledge with that of physics, mathematics, weather science, artificial satellites and so forth. - To nurture scientific temper by eradicating superstitions related to astronomical objects and events like planets, sun, moon and eclipses. - To correlate our heritage and culture with science.
sections.eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society or Authority promoted by the State or Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 1, that is, a city or town with a population of 15,00,000 or more, and the planetarium shall have a 12 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 2, that is, a city or town with a population between 5,00,000 and 15,00,000, and the planetarium shall have a 10 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 3, that is, a city, town or location with a population of less than 5,00,000, and the planetarium shall have an 8 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 2.0 acres of land, or 1.0 acre if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 2.0 acres of land, or 1.0 acre if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 1.0 acre of land. 1. The applicant may either collocate the Centre with an existing Science Centre, or attach it to one, or set it up independently in another non-formal educational institution which is engaged in science popularization activities. 1. The applicant State Government or Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for the operation and management of the Digital Planetarium. 1. The applicant should obtain all other statutory clearances and approvals required by the local authorities of the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory Government or other bodies. 1. The applicant should choose the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, the National Council of Science Museums. 1. The applicant should not change the land once offered; if any such incident is noticed after release of grant by the Ministry, the released amount shall be recovered from the organisation with the applicable rate of interest. 1. The applicant should provide provisions for the solar rooftop in the Detailed Project Report, which is mandatory for the implementing agency. 1. The applicant should ensure that all buildings constructed under the scheme are designed keeping applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should form a Registered Society immediately after the release of the fund by the State Governments or Union Territories towards their share of the capital cost of the project. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Council of Science Museums for implementation of the project, if undertaken and implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Preference, Priority and Relaxation:** - The land requirement is relaxed to 1.0 acre for Category 1 and Category 2 if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. - The Digital Planetarium is to be preferably co-located in the existing Science Centres, science museums or non-formal education institutions that promote science communication, especially astronomy education. - Preferably, the State Government, Union Territory, or agency shall undertake the construction of the building within the allocated budget, with inputs and supervision from the National Council of Science Museums. - The eligibility criteria of population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability of the project considering the intangible outcome of the facility in terms of knowledge gain may be relaxed and/or modified in special cases or circumstances by the Honourable Chief Minister, Government of India, as stated in the document. - In the construction of the building, priority or preference may be given to local material, labour and expertise; wherever possible, community participation may be encouraged; use of renewable energy and energy-saving devices may be given top preference.

The capital cost includes Civil and allied works ₹4.02 crore; Chairs ₹0.15 crore; Air Conditioning of Planetarium theatre and exhibition areas only ₹0.50 crore; Carpet in planetarium theatre ₹0.06 crore; Firefighting System ₹0.25 crore; Pure Digital Full-dome solution with High Contrast Light Emitting Diode or Solid State light source projection system with effective resolution of 4.5K after blending, including cost of 12.0 Metre Diameter inner Aluminium Dome ₹10.00 crore; Uninterruptible Power Supply ₹0.15 crore; Telescope and accessories for sky observations ₹1.00 crore; Office furniture, furnishing and tools ₹0.25 crore; Exhibits on Astronomy within the circular passage around the planetarium theatre with exhibition space of 350 Square Metres approximately ₹1.00 crore; Transportation, Installation and Commissioning of Exhibits at site ₹0.20 crore; Travelling Allowance or Daily Allowance, Training and Miscellaneous Expenditure ₹0.20 crore; and Architects Fee ₹0.22 crore.- **Category 2**: Main Opto-mechanical Star field Projector capable of projecting 8,500 stars down to 6.5 magnitude. Dome Size 10 metre diameter; Seating Capacity 80 to 85 unidirectional. Dome Size 8 metre diameter; Seating Capacity 50 unidirectional. The capital cost includes Civil and allied works ₹2.22 crore; Chairs ₹0.06 crore; Air Conditioning ₹0.30 crore; Carpet ₹0.02 crore; Firefighting equipment, standalone using portable fire extinguisher ₹0.20 crore; Single projector fish eye lens equipment with effective resolution 2K ₹1.00 crore; 8 Metre Diameter Inner Aluminium Dome ₹1.00 crore; Uninterruptible Power Supply ₹0.05 crore; Telescope and accessories ₹0.06 crore; Office furniture ₹0.10 crore; Exhibits on Astronomy with exhibition space of 200 Square Metres approximately ₹0.75 crore; Transportation, installation and commissioning ₹0.10 crore; Travelling Allowance or Daily Allowance, Training and Miscellaneous expenditure ₹0.12 crore; and Architects Fee ₹0.12 crore. - **Additional Items for Category 1 and Category 2:** Special Effect Projectors and Attachments; Complete sound system for the Planetarium Theatre; Projection dome; and Cove lights. - **Additional Facilities for Category 1 and Category 2:** Interactive exhibition on astronomy and space science; Activity area for students on astronomy; Sky observation through a Global Positioning System-enabled telescope; Lecture hall for astronomy lectures by specialists; and Office, maintenance workshop, and show development room. - **Additional Facilities for Category 3:** Activity area for students on astronomy; Sky observation through a Global Positioning System-enabled telescope; Lecture hall for astronomy lectures by specialists; and Office, maintenance workshop and show development room. > **Mode of Disbursement:** Normally, the digital planetarium will be set up by the National Council of Science Museums on a turn-key basis, including construction and commissioning of the equipment, and handed over after completion to the State Government or Union Territory. The construction work shall start only after the share or funding is received from the State or Union Territory Government. Preferably, the construction of the building shall be undertaken by the State Government, Union Territory or agency within the allocated budget as per inputs and supervision by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Frequency of Disbursement — Year-wise Utilization of Capital Expenditure:** For all three categories, the capital expenditure is released at 60 per cent in the first year and 40 per cent in the second year.

sections.how_to_apply: ### Offline **Step 1:** Determine the Category 1 with a 12 metre dome at a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre Category 1, Category 2 with a 10 metre dome at a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre Category 2, and Category 3 with an 8 metre dome at a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre Category 3, and confirm the land availability of 2.0 acres, 2.0 acres and 1.0 acre respectively, or 1.0 acre for Category 1 and Category 2 if inside the Science Centre Campus. **Step 2:** Decide the funding Type A, Type B (shared 50:50, or 90:10 for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim, with corpus fund 20:80) or Type C (full State funding with technical support against consultancy charges). **Step 3:** Select the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, the National Council of Science Museums; the land cannot be changed later, otherwise the released amount shall be recovered with applicable interest. **Step 4:** Obtain the Detailed Project Report format at [Annexure E](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf), with [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) for the Physical Report on Site. **Step 5:** Prepare the Detailed Project Report, including the feasibility report, demand survey for the need of the facility at the location, commitment of land free of cost and the recurring cost, projected footfall and expected revenue generation, to determine whether the proposed Digital Planetarium is viable and financially self-sustainable. It will preferably be a hardbound volume in A4 size in portrait alignment; an incomplete Detailed Project Report will render the application liable for rejection. **Step 6:** Attach the mandatory documents, along with the filled [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) with Site Map, Google Map and Non-Encumbrance Certificate. **Step 7:** Submit the proposal with the Detailed Project Report to: > _Joint Secretary (Museums)_ > _Ministry of Culture, Government of India,_ > _Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi-110001_ **Step 8:** The proposal shall be considered on the basis of challenge method guidelines, as and when issued by the Government of India, and per the criteria and parameters prescribed for the purpose in the scheme. **Step 9:** The Detailed Project Report will be appraised by the Project Appraisal Committee, comprising the Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Director or Deputy Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Representative from the Integrated Finance Division, Ministry of Culture; Director General, National Council of Science Museums; and Director, National Council of Science Museums dealing with the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science, for further recommendation to obtain approval of the competent authority. **Step 10:** Obtain approval from the Government of India for setting up the Digital Planetarium under the scheme. **Step 11:** Sign the Memorandum of Understanding between the National Council of Science Museums and the State or Union Territory Government for implementation of the project, if undertaken and implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. **Step 12:** Form the Registered Society immediately after the release of the fund by the State Governments or Union Territories towards their share of the capital cost of the project. A representative of the National Council of Science Museums shall be an ex-officio member of this Society or its Governing Council. The Society shall ensure that the Planetarium functions as per the requirements of its objectives without any deviations. The corpus fund share is released upfront after approval of the project and prior to commencement of the works. **Step 13:** Normally, the digital planetarium will be set up by the National Council of Science Museums on a turnkey basis, and construction shall start only after the share or funding is received from the State or Union Territory Government. Preferably, the construction of the building shall be undertaken by the State Government, Union Territory or agency within the allocated budget as per inputs and supervision by the National Council of Science Museums. **Step 14:** The Registered Society shall complete the recruitment of the required core staff members within 6 months of the release of funds, with the National Council of Science Museums providing professional support to the Executive Council for recruitment and training of staff, the cost of training being borne by the Society. The required staff strength is as follows: - **Category 1 and Category 2, total 6 posts:** To be recruited and posted within 3 months after the commencement of the project — Curator or Education Officer, Master of Science (1); Education assistant, Bachelor of Science (1); Lower Division Clerk (1). To be recruited and posted during the installation of the equipment in the planetarium — Technical Assistant, Diploma (1); Technicians, Electronics 1 and Electrical 1 (2).- **Category 3, total 4 posts:** To be recruited and posted within 3 months after the commencement of the project — Education Officer, Master of Science, or Education Assistant, Bachelor of Science (1); Lower Division Clerk (1). To be recruited and posted during the installation of the equipment in the planetarium — Technicians, Electronics 1 and Electrical 1 (2).- Security and Conservancy shall be run on contract. The National Council of Science Museums shall provide an organic link for the activities and upgradation, and will train the staff members recruited by the Society for the Centre. **Step 15:** Complete the project within 24 months from the date of issue of the Letter of Intent for the construction work, that is, 24 months from the date of commencement of construction. **Step 16:** Monitoring of Digital Planetariums set up as individual Autonomous Societies under Type B and Type C shall be done by an Executive Council set up by the respective State or Union Territory Government, with due representation from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, the National Council of Science Museums, the concerned State Government, their private or corporate partners if any, and at least five eminent personalities in the fields of education, Astrophysics, Science and Technology, industry and Science Communication, for recruitment of staff, budgeting, planning and execution of the Annual Plan of activities of the digital planetarium. In case the planetarium is set up in the existing science centres, the existing Executive Council shall monitor the working of the digital planetarium. **Step 17: T**he Digital Planetarium or Space and Astronomy Education Centres will be operated and maintained by a Registered Society formed by the State Government for this purpose. The Planetarium shall be run by an agency or society formed for this purpose or by a suitable Society. Over 5 years from opening, it should generate at least 50 per cent of its operating cost, achieve an annual footfall of around 1,00,000 for Category 1 (75,000 for the North East Region), around 75,000 for Category 2 (50,000 for the North East Region) and around 25,000 for Category 3, and organise a minimum of 5 to 10 astronomy education programmes in a year. > **Jurisdiction:** All disputes arising out of the scheme shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Courts of Delhi and New Delhi only.

name: Scheme For Promotion Of Culture Of Science: Innovation Hubs
summary: The "Innovation Hubs" component of the Scheme aims to foster problem-solving, project-based learning, and innovation among young children. Capital and three-year recurring assistance on a 50:50 sharing basis is provided to State/Union Territory Governments, Societies and institutions.

sections.overview: The component "Innovation Hubs" under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to redefine the usage and role of existing science facilities in fostering problem-solving and project-based learning, and to provide hands-on and practical learning and engagement in the process of science, technology and innovation. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and recurring cost for the first three years is provided to State Governments, Union Territories, Societies and institutions, on a 50:50 sharing basis. Innovation Hubs would be co-located in existing Science Cities/Science Centres, science museums and non-formal educational institutions that promote creativity and inspire innovations; this co-location would promote more effective utilisation of these centres. The hubs would serve as springboards for new ideas and innovation, thus helping society and the economy to face future challenges and meet rising aspirations of the growing population. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To equip and strengthen activities of the existing Science Cities/Science Centres/institutions to inspire innovations by young children. - To catalyse creation of more innovation hubs in different parts of the country, especially in rural areas. - To provide an appropriate environment to nurture creative and innovative ideas of young children.
sections.eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society/Authority promoted by the State/Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant should preferably co-locate the Innovation Hub in an existing Science City, Science Centre, science museum or non-formal education institution that promotes creativity and inspires innovations. 1. The applicant should provide a minimum of 1.0 acre of land. 1. The applicant should note that the land shall be provided free of cost by the host institution/State Government. 1. The applicant should note that approximately 300 square metres of built-up area is required for the facilities. 1. The applicant should indicate the availability of built-up space of 300 square metres in the application form. 1. The applicant should indicate the Category of the Innovation Hub applied for, that is, Category 1 (without built-up space) or Category 2 (with built-up space). 1. The applicant State Government/Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for operation and management. 1. The applicant should obtain all other statutory clearances and approvals required by the local authorities. 1. The applicant should provide provisions for the solar rooftop in the Detailed Project Report. 1. The applicant should ensure that buildings are designed keeping in view applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should deploy adequate manpower from the existing staff for the operation of the Innovation Hub and induct mentors for guiding the students. 1. The applicant, if the Innovation Hub is set up by a Society, should complete the recruitment of the required core staff members within 6 months of the release of funds. 1. The applicant should not change the land once offered; if any such incident is noticed after release of grant, the released amount shall be recovered with the applicable rate of interest. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with NCSM for implementation, if the project is undertaken and implemented by NCSM. > **Preference/Priority/Relaxation** - Even though support for constructing the 300 square metre space is available within the scheme, priority shall be given to institutions, science centres and museums who could offer ready-built space for the Innovation Hub. - In case the land is located in the heart of the city where land availability is scarce, the land requirement may be relaxed in the case of innovation hubs. The building may be constructed in multiple stories utilising the available Floor Space Ratio of the location. - Innovation Hubs are to be catalysed in different parts of the country, especially in rural areas. - Students from Government schools and colleges should be encouraged by giving concessional membership. - The eligibility criteria of population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability may be relaxed and/or modified in special cases/circumstances by the Honourable Chief Minister, Government of India, as stated in the document.
sections.benefits: > **Project Cost:** **Location****Capital Cost****Recurring Cost for 3 Years (at ₹0.20 crore per year)****Total Project Cost**All locations (Category 1, where space is to be constructed)₹2.60 crore₹0.60 crore₹3.20 croreAll locations (Category 2, where space is already constructed)₹1.50 crore₹0.60 crore₹2.10 crore> **Conditions Attached to the Benefit:** - The total project cost is to be shared in the ratio 50:50 between the State/Union Territory Government and the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and this includes the recurring cost of Innovation Hubs. - The capital cost for setting up a new Innovation Hub shall be ₹2.60 crore under Category 1; in case built-up space of approximately 300 square metres is available under Category 2, the capital cost would be ₹1.50 crore. - There is no Corpus Fund for Innovation Hubs, but a recurring grant is given for the initial three years. - The recurring cost for the first three years is at ₹10,00,000/- per year per hub as the 50 per cent share of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, after opening of the Innovation Hub; the balance 50 per cent is to be borne by the State Governments/Union Territories/Society. - The expected expenditure after inauguration of the Innovation Hub is ₹20,00,000/- per year. The share of recurring cost of the Government of India shall be available for the initial three years of operation as an incentive under the Scheme. After the initial three years of operation, the State Government/Union Territories/institutions will undertake to continue the activities. - The State Governments/Union Territories/Society/institutions have to bear the gap funding and the recurring cost thereafter. - The recurring expenditure, including the salary component, will be completely borne by the respective organisations. NCSM shall train the staff members on operation and maintenance of the Innovation Hubs. > **Facilities Created Under the Component:** Approximately 300 square metres built-up area would be required for setting up the following facilities: **Innovation Hubs Facilities****Space Requirement (Approx.)****Objective/Contents/Activities****Discovery Hall**100 M²This area will have 10 to 15 interactive science exhibits/experiments to create excitement about science through exploration and discovery of underlying principles. This will help promote logical thinking. **Innovation Resource Centre and Hall of Fame -** _Celebrating Inventions &amp;amp; Innovation_50 M²This space will be used to showcase innovative ideas/products/implements that have transformed our world or have made a significant impact on the way we conduct our lives, along with respective inventors &amp;amp; innovators. Stories or inspirations behind such innovations/inventions will also be mentioned through appropriate modes. Besides these, implements/ samples of appropriate technology and traditional knowledge systems, art and craft, and other areas of importance in public life in the respective regions shall be exhibited.**Idea Lab (Innovation Laboratory) with the following components: - ThodPhod Jod (Break &amp;amp; Remake) Corner - Kabbad Se Jugad (Build from scraps) - Idea Box**100 M²This lab will have the necessary basic facilities to pursue creative and innovative hobbies/activities that involve model making, basic science experimentation, design &amp;amp; fabrication of useful gadgets for practical use, teaching/learning kits or aids for better classroom transactions, and testing of samples like soil, water, food items, etc. Students learn to do things with their own hands, dismantle, reassemble and remake devices/gadgets. Students learn more by doing things practically using day-to-day scrap. Students generate their own innovative ideas and create an idea bank. The best ideas are chosen for experimentation/model making/project work.**Design Studio**50 M²**Mentors/Guides**At least one dedicated mentor on a contract basis. Additional mentoring support may be provided by NCSM centres.As far as possible, each institution shall try to provide mentoring and guidance support for innovation activities in its own centres. But that may not always be possible, and hence external experts in different fields will also be engaged on an honorarium basis. It would, however, be appropriate to engage on a contract basis at least one core mentor, who shall be primarily responsible for coordinating and conducting the innovation centre activities.> **Mode of Disbursement:** The State Governments/Union Territories/Institutions shall do the construction of the building/space for the Innovation Hub as per inputs from NCSM. NCSM shall provide technical and professional support at cost and consultancy charges to the State/Union Territory Government for the project. > **Expected Time of Completion:** - Completion time from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work – 24 months. - The time required for implementation of the Innovation Hub project will be 24 months from the start of the construction work where space is to be created, and 18 months where no space is required to be created. > **Validity/Post-Sanction Obligations:** After opening, the Innovation Hub should strive to enrol at least 300 active innovation members annually; increase the number of exposure visits to innovation hubs by school and college students and teachers to approximately 10,000 annually; file patents/copyrights on successful innovative prototypes; and set up at least 10 Innovation Clubs in nearby schools. > In addition, the Innovation Hubs should also strive to organize activities such as idea contests and innovation festivals including contests on design and idea challenges on local problems periodically; develop strong linkages with Indian Institutes of Technology, National Institutes of Technology, Universities, Research Institutions and Industry; and develop synergy with Atal Tinkering Labs by collaborating with such labs in schools and institutions across the country by way of exposure visits of student participants to the innovation hub facilities, sharing of success stories and training of mentors.

sections.how_to_apply: ### Offline **Step 1:** Confirm eligibility and category: The Innovation Hub is to be preferably co-located in existing Science Cities, Science Centres, science museums or non-formal education institutions that promote creativity and inspire innovations, with a minimum of 1.0 acre of land, provided free of cost by the host institution or State Government. Determine Category 1 (space is to be constructed) or Category 2 (built-up space of approximately 300 square metres is already available). **Step 2:** Obtain the Application Form for Grants-in-aid and the Detailed Project Report format, both enclosed at [Annexure F](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf). **Step 3:** Fill the application form with the name and complete address of the organization, availability of built up space of 300 square metres, category applied for, details of income from other sources including foreign sources during the last three financial years, estimated cost, own resources, amount of grant-in-aid sought, grants-in-aid sought or received from other bodies, location of site, past experience, projects taken up in the last 10 years, and organization and management of work. **Step 4:** Prepare the Detailed Project Report as per [Annexure F](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf), preferably as a hard-bound volume in A4 size in portrait alignment. An incomplete Detailed Project Report will render the application liable for rejection. **Step 5:** Attach the mandatory documents: Copy of Registration (in case of Societies), Memorandum of Association or Trust Deed (in case of Societies), Letter of Support from State Government, Letter of Recommendation from District Authority, Authorisation Certificate, Audited Statement of Accounts for last three years, and Commitments for space, operation and sustenance of the facility. **Step 6:** Certify that the information given is correct, and sign the form as applicant or Head of Organisation with name in block letters, designation and office stamp. **Step 7:** Submit the proposal with the Detailed Project Report to the Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture, Government of India, Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi-110001. **Step 8:** The Detailed Project Report is appraised by the National Level Committee constituted by the Ministry of Culture, which scrutinises the applications and Detailed Project Reports received along with necessary commitments from the respective State Government or parent organisation and recommends potentially viable projects. Mere applying for the grant-in-aid will not guarantee allocation; an innovative approach, a sustenance plan and activities will decide the merit of each proposal. **Step 9:** Obtain approval from the Government of India for setting up the Innovation Hub under the scheme. **Step 10:** Sign the Memorandum of Understanding with the National Council of Science Museums, if the project is undertaken and implemented by it. **Step 11:** Construction: the State Governments, Union Territories or Institutions shall do the construction of the building or space for the Innovation Hub as per inputs from the National Council of Science Museums, which shall provide technical and professional support at cost and consultancy charges. **Step 12:** Deploy manpower: the Science Cities, Science Centres or Institutions shall deploy adequate manpower from the existing staff for the operation of the Innovation Hub and induct mentors for guiding the students. In case it is set up by a Society, the Registered Society shall complete recruitment of the required core staff members within 6 months of the release of funds. At least one dedicated mentor is to be engaged on a contract basis. **Step 13:** Complete the project within 24 months from the date of issue of the Letter of Intent for the construction work, that is, 24 months from the start of construction where space is to be created and 18 months where no space is required to be created. **Step 14:** Monitoring is done by a local board constituted with representatives from industry associations, academia, civil society, research organisations and so forth, with a minimum of 5 members, and with a representative from the National Council of Science Museums. **Step 15:** After opening, achieve the Outcome Evaluation Indicators: enrol at least 300 active innovation members annually, increase exposure visits by school and college students and teachers to approximately 10,000 annually, file patents or copyrights on successful innovative prototypes, and set up at least 10 Innovation Clubs in nearby schools.

name: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Modernization/Up-gradation Of Existing Science Cities, Science Centres And Innovation Hubs
summary: The Scheme aims to modernise and upgrade galleries, exhibitions and visitor amenities in existing facilities. Grants up to specified maximum ceilings are provided to eligible existing Science Cities, Science Centres and Innovation Hubs.

sections.overview: The component "Modernization/Up-gradation of Existing Science Cities, Science Centres and Innovation Hubs" under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to provide grants and funds to modernise and upgrade, and to create a congenial spatial setting for diverse exhibitions, galleries and visitor amenities in the existing science cities, science centres and innovation hubs. Through this component, financial assistance up to a specified maximum ceiling is provided to those existing Science Cities, Science Centres and Innovation Hubs which were developed with funding from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, or developed by the State Governments and Union Territories with full funding. India has over 50 to 60 Science Museums, Centres and Cities functioning in different States and Union Territories, of which 49 have been developed by the National Council of Science Museums since 1959; 25 centres are managed by the National Council of Science Museums and the remaining 24 have been handed over to the respective States, Union Territories and Societies for operation and management. The existing science museums and centres developed in the past have varying architecture, facilities, content and infrastructure, some of which do not conform to the prevailing trends in the world; with rapid development in science and technology, communication techniques and digital technologies, the Science Centres and Cities require modernization and up-gradation commensurate with the modern trends and requirements. The Modernization or Up-gradation plan may also include addition of a Mobile Science Exhibition unit to an existing Science City or Science Centre. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums.
sections.eligibility: 1. The applicant should be an existing Science City, Science Centre or Innovation Hub. 1. The applicant should have been developed with funding from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, or developed by the State Government or Union Territories with full funding. 1. The applicant should have completed at least 5 years of operation. 1. The applicant should have satisfactory performance. 1. The applicant should submit a Detailed Project Report in the approved format, that is, [Annexure H](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf), to the Ministry of Culture.1. The applicant should propose facilities as per [Annexure G](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf).1. The applicant should obtain approval from the Government of India for modernization of the existing science city, centre or innovation hub under the scheme. 1. The applicant should indicate the availability of Built-Up Space in the application form. 1. The applicant should indicate the category of the Science City, Science Centre or Innovation Hub applied for. 1. The applicant should ensure that all buildings constructed under the scheme are designed keeping applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Council of Science Museums for implementation of the Project. 1. The applicant should sanction and release the State or Union Territory's share of funds from the respective State or Union Territory Government or Society. 1. The applicant should submit the utilization certificate for the funds released from the Government of India and the State Governments, Union Territories and Societies. 1. The applicant should certify that the information given in the application is correct, and undertake to abide by it on behalf of the organisation. > **Preference/Priority/Relaxation:** - The facilities to be added are subject to availability of space and spare land, within the funds sanctioned under the scheme. - In the construction of the building, priority or preference may be given to local material, labour and expertise. Also, wherever possible, community participation may be encouraged. Use of renewable energy and energy-saving devices may be given top preference.
sections.benefits: > **Total Funding, Sharing Pattern and Completion Time (₹ In Crore):** **Category****Total funding (Maximum)****Sharing of Funds between the Government of India and the State Government/Union Territory/Society****Project/Scheme completion time (Maximum)**Science City (All locations other than North East including Sikkim)36.2560:4036 monthsScience City in the North Eastern Region, including Sikkim State44.0090:1036 monthsScience Centres – Category 1 (All locations other than North East including Sikkim)7.2550:5024 monthsScience Centres – Category 1 in North Eastern Region including Sikkim State8.7090:1024 monthsScience Centres – Category 2 (All locations other than North East including Sikkim)3.6550:5024 monthsScience Centres – Category 2 in North Eastern Region including Sikkim State4.3590:1024 monthsScience Centres – Category 3 (All locations other than North East including Sikkim)2.2050:5018 monthsScience Centres – Category 3 in North Eastern Region including Sikkim State2.9090:1018 monthsInnovation Hubs1.5050:5012 months> **Facilities That May Be Added Under Modernization/Up-gradation:** The existing science cities and science centres may be modernised or upgraded with the following facilities, subject to availability of space and spare land, within the funds sanctioned under the scheme: - Modernization of Galleries, Exhibitions, Halls, Science Parks and visitors' amenities. - Addition of galleries on frontier areas of Science and Technology and topics related to current issues in Science. - Digital panoramic thematic presentations based on important scientific topics as well as on science and culture inter-relationship. - Addition of open labs on Frontier Areas of Science and Technology to provide real scientific exploration by the public. - Presentations on social issues with scientific solutions after proper contextualization. - Addition of virtual and immersive experiences. - Creation of new facilities such as Tropical Forests, Outdoor Amphi-Theatre, Solar powered park, Holography theatre, Hall of Fame to celebrate inventions and inventors, Digitally recreated archaeological sites, Spark Theatre, Dark Rides, Simulators, Robotics corner, 3D facility and Interpretation centres. - Addition of a mobile science exhibition van or bus on a suitable theme for travelling in rural and nearby region of the location. > **Conditions Associated with the Benefit:** - The actual budget will depend upon the facilities identified for up-gradation and modernization. - In no case shall the funds provided under the Modernization or Up-gradation scheme be utilized for acquiring land or an office vehicle for the Science Centre or City. - The Modernization or Up-gradation plan may also include addition of a Mobile Science Exhibition unit to an existing Science City or Science Centre. - The National Council of Science Museums shall be paid normal consultancy fees for execution of the project, or for the purpose where the project is implemented by the concerned Societies. - All buildings constructed under the scheme should be designed keeping applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. > **Mode of Disbursement:** - The project shall normally be undertaken by the National Council of Science Museums on a turn-key basis. The funds for the project will be received by the National Council of Science Museums, both from the Central Government and the State Governments, Union Territories and Societies. The National Council of Science Museums shall take up the modernization or up-gradation of the Science Cities, Centres and Innovation Hubs on its own, or through Creative Museum Designers, a wholly owned Section 25 company of the National Council of Science Museums. - In case of a State or Union Territory Government, or the Societies formed by the State or Union Territory Governments, seeking financial support from the Government of India for a modernization or up-gradation project to be implemented by the concerned Societies, the project will be vetted and processed by the National Council of Science Museums for approval of the competent authority in the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. > **Frequency of Disbursement:** - In such a case, funds will be released by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, to the State Government or Union Territory, or to the Societies, in a phased manner, subject to sanction and release of the State or Union Territory's share of funds from the respective State or Union Territory Governments and Societies, and submission of the utilization certificate by the State or Union Territory Government and Societies for the funds released from the Government of India and the State Governments, Union Territories and Societies. > **Expected Time of Completion:** - The maximum project or scheme completion time is 36 months for a Science City, 24 months for Science Centres Category 1 and Category 2, 18 months for Science Centres Category 3, and 12 months for Innovation Hubs.

Where the project is to be implemented by the concerned Societies, the project will be vetted and processed by the National Council of Science Museums for approval of the competent authority in the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. **Step 10:** Obtain approval from the Government of India for modernization of the existing science city, centre or innovation hub under the scheme. **Step 11:** Sign the Memorandum of Understanding between the National Council of Science Museums and the State Government, Union Territory or Society for implementation of the Project. **Step 12:** Where the project is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums, funds are received by it from both the Central Government and the State Governments, Union Territories and Societies. name: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Science City
summary: The scheme aims to create an immersive, experiment-based learning attraction that builds scientific temper. Financial assistance for capital cost and corpus fund is provided to State/Union Territory Governments and their Societies.

sections.overview: The component "Science City" under the "Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science" by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to create a popular tourist attraction at the location that provides an experiment-based immersive learning ambience to inculcate a spirit of inquiry, foster creative talent and create scientific temper in the community as a whole. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and corpus fund is provided to State Governments, Union Territories, and the Societies/Authorities promoted by them. A Science City is characterised by its two-pronged channel of communication, namely exhibits and activities; while the exhibits, both indoor and outdoor, are mostly interactive, the demonstrations and training programmes are fully participatory and help children and adults alike to learn the basics of science through fun and enjoyment. It will be large in dimension with a focus on frontier areas of Science and Technology and edutainment, and shall be financially self-sustainable. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To portray the growth of science and technology and their application in industry and human welfare, with a view to developing a scientific attitude and temper. - To create awareness and enhance public understanding, appreciation and engagement of the public in the process of Science and Technology. - To popularise science and technology by organising exhibitions, seminars, popular lectures, science camps and various other programmes. - To supplement science education given in schools and colleges, and to organise out-of-school educational activities. - To design, develop and fabricate science museum exhibits, demonstration equipment and scientific teaching aids. - To organise training programmes for science teachers, students, young entrepreneurs, technicians, physically challenged persons, housewives and others.
sections.eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society/Authority promoted by the State/Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant should propose a location, preferably where no major Science Centre exists. 1. The applicant may alternatively propose upgradation of an existing science centre to a Science City in locations where footfall to the science centre is substantial. 1. The applicant may alternatively propose a separate Science City in a State capital or the largest city of the State, provided that the Science City is viable and financially self-sustainable. 1. The applicant should provide at least 25.0 acres of land; however, 30.0 acres would be preferable to do justice to exhibits and facilities, especially those requiring open spaces and future expansion. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is preferably centrally located, easily accessible, fully developed, without any low-lying area, of fairly regular shape, and secured with a boundary wall without any encumbrances. 1. The applicant State Government/Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for operation and management. 1. The applicant should obtain all other statutory clearances and approvals required by the local authorities of the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory Government or other bodies. 1. The applicant should choose the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, NCSM. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is free from all encumbrances and encroachment. 1. The applicant should ensure that electricity, water, sewerage connection and telecommunication facilities are available in the nearby vicinity. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land has good road connectivity for easy access and transport. 1. The applicant should not change the land once offered; if any such incident is noticed after release of grant, the released amount shall be recovered from the organisation with the applicable rate of interest. 1. The applicant should provide provisions for the solar rooftop in the Detailed Project Report, which is mandatory for the implementing agency. 1. The applicant should ensure that buildings are designed keeping in view applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with NCSM for implementation, if the project is undertaken and implemented by NCSM. 1. The applicant should form the Society before the start of execution of the project so that it is able to receive monetary grants from both Central and State/Union Territory Governments, private/corporate/industry sources, as well as raise loans from financial institutions.
sections.benefits: > **Project Cost:** **Location****Capital Cost****Corpus Fund****Total Project Cost**All locations other than North Eastern Region including Sikkim, Hilly Terrain and Island territories₹179.00 crore₹53.70 crore₹232.70 croreNorth Eastern Region including Sikkim₹214.80 crore₹64.50 crore₹279.30 croreHilly Terrain and Island Territories other than location in North Eastern Region including Sikkim₹214.80 crore₹64.50 crore₹279.30 crore> **Conditions Attached to the Benefit:** 1. A Science City is not to be set up under Type A funding, that is, full funding from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. 1. Under Type B funding, the capital cost is shared on a 60:40 basis between the Government of India and the State Government/Union Territory, except for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim, where it is shared on a 90:10 basis. 1. The corpus fund is shared 20:80 between the Government of India and the State Government/Union Territory; the Government of India share shall in no case exceed 20 per cent of the total Corpus Fund. 1. Under Type C funding, the State Government/Union Territory fully funds the project and sets it up with technical support from NCSM against payment of consultancy charges. 1. The corpus fund meets the operational deficit funding. The principal shall in no case be utilised for any activity. Not more than 85 per cent of the interest can be utilised to meet the operational deficit after inauguration, and a minimum of 15 per cent is to be added back to the corpus fund to compensate for inflation on a year to year basis. 1. The recurring expenditure is completely borne by the State/Union Territory Government, except where the Government of India decides to fully fund the project and manage it through NCSM. 1. Pile foundation, if required, will be considered after getting the Soil Test Report; the additional cost is entirely borne by the State Government. 1. Third-party quality assurance charges at 1 per cent of the estimated cost are entirely borne by the State Government. 1. Escalation of project cost is governed by the successive cost index over DPAR-2019 as published by the Central Public Works Department; the extra cost is borne by the State Government/local authority. > **Indicative Break-up of the Capital Cost:** 1. **Expenditure on Building construction works:** Grand Total ₹110.81 crore, which includes Science Centre building of 14,000 square metres minimum with indoor exhibition halls, internal electrification, external Light Emitting Diode lighting, water supply and sanitary installation, firefighting, car and bus parking, underground reservoir of 2,50,000 litres, lifts, escalators, air-conditioning, Diesel Generator set, Closed Circuit Television surveillance, chairs and carpet, contingency at 3 per cent as per Central Public Works Department norms, and architect fee.1. **Expenditure on Exhibits, Equipment and Stores:** Grand Total ₹68.00 crore, which includes large format film projection unit with laser projectors and accessories (₹25.00 crore), simulator and 3D film theatre (₹4.00 crore), thematic exhibits for Face to Face with Science and Technology (₹8.00 crore), interactive exhibits for experimentation and curriculum supplement (₹2.00 crore), projection equipment for auditorium (₹1.00 crore) and for digital panorama with laser projectors (₹22.00 crore), workshop tools and machineries (₹1.00 crore), development of Science park exhibits (₹1.50 crore), salary of project staff (₹2.50 crore), Travelling Allowance/Daily Allowance for project staff (₹0.40 crore), other administrative expenses (₹0.40 crore), and advertisement and publicity (₹0.20 crore).1. **Corpus Fund for Operational Deficit funding after inauguration:** at 30 per cent of the project cost.**Mode of Disbursement:** 1. The project shall normally be undertaken by NCSM on a turn-key basis. The funds are received by NCSM, both from the Central Government and the State Governments/Union Territories. NCSM sets up the Science City and hands it over to the State Government/Society for operation and management. 1. In case a State/Union Territory Government seeks financial support for a project to be implemented by themselves, a society should be formed by the respective State/Union Territory Government, and funds will be released by the Government of India to the society based on the recommendations of a Project Implementation Committee constituted by the Ministry of Culture with representatives of the Ministry of Culture, NCSM, experts in the field and the State Government. > **Frequency of Disbursement — Year-wise Utilization of Capital Expenditure:** 1. **For all locations other than North East including Sikkim/hilly terrain and island territories:** 15 per cent in the first year, 25 per cent in the second year, 25 per cent in the third year, 25 per cent in the fourth year, and 10 per cent in the fifth year. The Government of India releases ₹16.11 crore, ₹26.85 crore, ₹26.85 crore, ₹26.85 crore and ₹10.74 crore respectively, totalling ₹107.40 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹10.74 crore, making ₹118.14 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹114.56 crore upfront prior to starting of the project, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹42.96 crore.1. **For North Eastern Region including Sikkim:** The Government of India releases ₹29.00 crore, ₹48.33 crore, ₹48.33 crore, ₹48.33 crore and ₹19.33 crore, totalling ₹193.32 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹12.90 crore, making ₹206.22 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹73.08 crore upfront, including the minimum share of the corpus fund of ₹51.60 crore.1. **For hilly terrains and island territories other than the above:** The Government of India releases ₹19.33 crore, ₹32.22 crore, ₹32.22 crore, ₹32.22 crore and ₹12.89 crore, totalling ₹128.88 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹12.90 crore, making ₹141.78 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹137.52 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹51.60 crore. 1. The share of the corpus fund of the Government of India and the State Government/Union Territory is to be released upfront after approval of the project and prior to commencement of the works. > **Expected Time of Completion:** 1. Completion time from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work 60 months. 1. Project timeline from the date of placing of order for construction of building: Construction of building including space theatre, science exploration hall, panorama and so forth 48 months; Development of Entrance Plaza 12 months; Development of Science Park 36 months; Fabrication of exhibits 30 months; Installation of exhibits 12 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre 60 months approximately. **Validity/Post-Sanction Obligations:** 1. Over a period of 5 years from opening, the Science City should strive to generate at least 50 per cent of its operating cost, achieve an annual visitors footfall of around 10,00,000 (5,00,000 for the North East Region), and organize a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually, in-house and outreach, including activities on climate change, biodiversity, nature conservation, topical issues and skill development.

sections.how_to_apply: ### Offline **Step 1:** Check basic criteria. Confirm the location criteria (preferably where no major Science Centre exists, or a State capital/largest city of the State, provided the Science City is viable and financially self-sustainable) and the land criteria of at least 25.0 acres, preferably 30.0 acres. **Step 2:** Decide the funding type. Only Type B (shared 60:40, or 90:10 for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim; corpus fund 20:80) or Type C (full State funding with technical support from the National Council of Science Museums against consultancy charges). A Science City is not to be set up under Type A. **Step 3:** Select the land with approval of the National Council of Science Museums. The land shall be chosen in consultation with, and with the approval of, the National Council of Science Museums, and cannot be changed later; otherwise the released amount shall be recovered with applicable interest. **Step 4:** Obtain the format. The Detailed Project Report format is enclosed with the guidelines at [Annexure E](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf), with [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) for the Physical Report on Site. **Step 5:** Prepare the Detailed Project Report. It should include the feasibility report, demand survey, commitment of land free of cost and recurring cost, projected footfall, and expected revenue generation. It will preferably be a hard-bound volume in A4 size in portrait alignment, with A3 drawings as foldouts. An incomplete Detailed Project Report will render the application liable for rejection. **Step 6:** Attach mandatory documents: Copy of Registration, Memorandum of Association or Trust Deed, Letter of Support from State Government, Letter of Recommendation from District Authority, Authorisation Certificate, Commitments for space and operation, and Audited Statement of Accounts for last three years, along with the filled [Annexure E-1](https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf) with Site Map, Google Map and Non-Encumbrance Certificate. **Step 7:** Submit the proposal to _Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture, Government of India, Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi-110001_ **Step 8:** Challenge method consideration. The proposal shall be considered on the basis of challenge method guidelines, as and when issued by the Government of India. **Step 9:** Appraisal by the Project Appraisal Committee, comprising the Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Director/Deputy Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Representative from the Integrated Finance Division, Ministry of Culture; Director General, National Council of Science Museums; and Director, National Council of Science Museums dealing with SPoCS. **Step 10:** Approval from the Government of India is required for setting up the Science City. Population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability may be relaxed in special cases. **Step 11:** Sign the Memorandum of Understanding between the National Council of Science Museums and the State/Union Territory Government, if implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. **Step 12:** Form the Society before the start of execution of the project, by the State/Union Territory Government in consultation with the National Council of Science Museums, so that it can receive grants and raise loans. **Step 13:** Release funds and begin construction. Funds are received by the National Council of Science Museums from both Central and State Governments, where it implements the project on a turn-key basis; where the State implements it, funds are released to the society on the recommendations of a Project Implementation Committee. The corpus fund share is released upfront after approval and prior to commencement of works. The State/Union Territory Government releases ₹114.56 crore, ₹73.08 crore or ₹137.52 crore upfront depending on location. **Step 14:** Recruit staff: 22 posts within 6 months of release of funds and 22 posts within two years, totalling 44 posts. **Step 15:** Execute as per the timeline 60 months from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work. **Step 16:** Monitoring by an Executive Council set up by the State/Union Territory Government with representation from the Ministry of Culture, the National Council of Science Museums, the State Government, private or corporate partners, and at least five eminent personalities. **Step 17:** Handover and outcome evaluation. The National Council of Science Museums hands over the Science City to the State Government/Society for operation and management. Over 5 years from opening, it should generate at least 50 per cent of operating cost, achieve an annual footfall of around 10,00,000 (5,00,000 for the North East Region), and organise a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually.

sections.overview: "Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region" by the Rubber Board, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The Scheme is intended to increase the production of natural rubber in India by accelerating new planting and replanting of rubber on scientific lines. Accelerated new planting/replanting would be achieved by giving proper technical guidance and financial assistance to growers.
sections.eligibility:
> **Traditional** 1. The growers owning rubber areas not exceeding 2.00 ha shall be eligible for assistance under Rule VI of the scheme. 1. The planting grant payable will be limited to an area of 1.00 ha. 1. The growers who undertake new planting/replanting rubber in a minimum area of 0.10 ha will be eligible for assistance. 1. The applicant should have absolute possession over the land in respect of which assistance is sought. 1. Areas notified/certified in the documents as paddy fields are not eligible for any kind of assistance under this scheme.
> **Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region** 1. The growers owning rubber areas not exceeding 5.00 ha shall be eligible for assistance under Rule VI of the scheme. 1. The planting grant payable will be limited to an area of 2.00 ha. 1. The growers who undertake new planting/replanting rubber in a minimum area of 0.10 ha will be eligible for assistance. 1. The applicant should have absolute possession over the land in respect of which assistance is sought. 1. Areas notified/certified in the documents as paddy fields are not eligible for any kind of assistance under this scheme.
> **Other Terms & Conditions** 1. The prescribed minimum stand of rubber plants (@450/ha) should be maintained and growth should be satisfactory as assessed by the inspecting officer. 1. The number of non-rubber trees, that already exist in the plantation can be retained in a proportion of 20 trees or 40 coconut palms or 80 Arecanut palms per ha, in a well-distributed manner. 1. Sloppy lands should be protected from soil erosion by contour terracing or construction of contour bunds or digging silt trenches or silt pits and also by planting of cover crops. 1. Boundary protection measures should be adopted. 1. The absolute right to refuse assistance without assigning any reason is vested with the Executive Director of the Rubber Board.
sections.benefits:
##### **Rate of Subsidy**
> **Traditional Region** 1. **General Category:** ₹ 20,000/- ha + ₹ 5,000 /ha for planting material (Polybag/ Root trainer plants) of advanced growth. The assistance will be @ ₹ 10/- per plant limited to 500 plants per ha.1. **SC Category:** ₹ 35000/- ha + ₹ 5,000 /ha for planting material (Polybag/ Root trainer plants) of advanced growth. The assistance will be @ ₹ 10/- per plant limited to 500 plants per ha.
> **Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region** 1. ₹ 35,000 per ha and ₹ 5,000/ ha for planting material (Polybag/ Root trainer plants) of advanced growth. 1. The assistance will be @ ₹ 10/- per plant limited to 500 plants per ha. ##### **Mode of Payment** 1. Planting subsidy shall be paid in single instalments subject to the completion of the stipulated items of work to the satisfaction of the Board. 1. Payment of subsidy shall be only through bank by e-transfer. Beneficiaries should provide Aadhar-linked bank account details in the application for financial assistance.

name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
summary: The scheme aims to offset the disability for domestic manufacturing of components and semiconductors to strengthen the electronics manufacturing ecosystem. Through this scheme, a financial incentive of 25% on capital expenditure to legal entities registered in India.

sections.overview: The scheme "Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)" has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) (Industrial Promotion — Electronics Hardware Manufacturing (IPHW) Division), Government of India, aims to help offset the disability for domestic manufacturing of electronic components and semiconductors to strengthen the electronics manufacturing ecosystem in the country, in alignment with the National Policy on Electronics 2019 (NPE 2019) and the Government's "Make in India" and "Digital India" programmes. Through this scheme, a financial incentive of 25% of capital expenditure (on a reimbursement basis) is provided to any legal entity registered in India investing in eligible electronic components, semiconductor/display fabrication units, Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) units, specialised sub-assemblies, and capital goods for manufacture of the aforesaid goods — covering both new units and expansion of capacity/modernisation and diversification of existing units. The scheme is implemented by MeitY through a Nodal Agency appointed as the Project Management Agency (PMA), which is responsible for receipt of applications, appraisal, issuance of acknowledgements, verification of claims, and disbursement of incentives; applications received under the scheme are appraised on an ongoing basis by the PMA, which places eligible applications before the Executive Committee (EC) constituted by MeitY, chaired by an officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary.
sections.eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a legal entity registered in India. The applicant may be a Private Limited Company, Public Limited Company, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership registered in India. 1. The applicant should be proposing to invest in a project/unit for the manufacturing of eligible goods as per the list in [Annexure-1](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/SPECS-Guidelines-01062020.pdf) of the SPECS Guidelines.1. Each application shall be treated as a new investment and as an independent application. The application shall be only for single-phase projects; phase-wise applications shall not be considered under the Scheme. 1. There is no restriction on any applicant from making multiple applications and/or for multiple locations. 1. The applicant should ensure that the proposed investment in capital expenditure is greater than or equal to the threshold value for the eligible goods under SPECS (as per [Annexure-1](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/SPECS-Guidelines-01062020.pdf) of the Guidelines). 1. The scheme is applicable for investments in new units as well as expansion of capacity/modernisation and/or diversification of existing units. 1. The minimum investment thresholds are the same for new units or expansion of capacity/modernisation/diversification of existing units. 1. A project/unit proposed under the Scheme may include multiple manufacturing facilities at one or more proposed locations. There is no limit on the number of applications for an applicant. 1. If an application covers more than one product category, the applicable minimum threshold of investment (capital expenditure) shall be the highest of the individual threshold investment for each of the product categories covered. 1. Eligibility under the SPECS Scheme shall not affect eligibility under any other scheme, and vice-versa. 1. The application shall contain the requisite land documents such as a registered sale deed and/or registered rent/lease agreement on the land for a period of not less than 10 years from the date of application in usual circumstances. 1. In case land has been taken on rent/lease for a period less than 10 years, such application shall be processed if there is a renewal clause for extension of the rent/lease agreement in the registered document. If the renewal clause is not present, the application may be referred by the Project Management Agency (PMA) to the Governing Council (GC) for an appropriate decision. 1. In case the land has not been purchased or taken on rent/lease at the time of application, the applicant shall provide definite location/plot details and a suitable document confirming availability of the land; however, the final registered document shall be provided before the submission of the Appraisal Report by PMA for consideration of the Executive Committee (EC). 1. The application shall contain a Financial Closure for the investment required for the complete project. Financial Closure means: - Firm commitment from the applicant to invest in the project under SPECS in the form of a Board Resolution. - Sanction letter/Letter of Intent (LoI) from a Bank/Financial Institution (FI)/loan agreement with Bank/FI for the debt portion of the investment proposed. - Legally binding commitment from equity/unsecured loan providers to provide or mobilise funds, in the form of an agreement backed by a Board Resolution (Board Resolution is not applicable in case of Banks and Financial Institutions; in that case, a sanction letter and/or LoI from the Bank/Financial Institution may be provided). - Legally binding commitment of funding from internal accruals (applicable in case the applicant has any existing unit; shall be assessed from past performance, including Profit and Loss Account, Cash Flow Statements, etc.). - Documents showing capability of fund providers in the form of unencumbered liquid funds (not applicable in case of Banks and Financial Institutions).
sections.benefits:
> **Financial Incentive:** • A financial incentive of 25% of eligible capital expenditure is provided to approved units manufacturing goods as per the eligible list annexed to the Scheme. • The total incentive under the Scheme is 25% of eligible capital expenditure for an approved application. • The incentive is over and above any incentive offered by the State Government or any of its agencies or local bodies. • Applicants shall also be eligible to take benefit under any other scheme(s) of the Government of India; however, investments committed under the Modified Special Incentive Package Scheme (M-SIPS) for which incentives have been claimed shall not qualify as eligible investments under SPECS. > **What Constitutes Eligible Capital Expenditure** Capital expenditure includes the following: • Expenditure on plant, machinery, equipment and associated utilities — including tools, dies, moulds, jigs, fixtures (including parts, accessories, components, and spares thereof); expenditure on packaging, freight/transport, insurance, and erection and commissioning. Associated utilities include captive power and effluent treatment plants; clean rooms; air curtains; temperature and air quality control systems; compressed air, water and power supply; and IT/ITES infrastructure related to manufacturing including servers, software and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solutions. • Expenditure on Research and Development (R&D) — including in-house and captive R&D, test and measuring instruments, design tools, software cost (directly for R&D), and expenditure on technology, Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), patents and copyrights. • Expenditure on Transfer of Technology (ToT) — including cost of technology and initial technology purchase related to eligible goods. • Expenditure on refurbished/used/second-hand plant, machinery and equipment (including associated utilities and R&D) — whether imported or domestically procured — not exceeding 20% of total eligible plant, machinery and equipment. Such equipment must have a minimum residual life of at least 5 (five) years at the time of transfer of assets. The following are NOT covered as eligible capital expenditure • Expenditure on land and building (including factory building/construction). • Expenditure on consumables and raw materials used for manufacturing. > **Sub-Limits within Eligible Capital Expenditure** • Associated utilities expenditure: capped at not more than 20% of the total eligible capital expenditure for plant, machinery and equipment. • Research and Development (R&D) expenditure: not exceeding 20% of the total eligible capital expenditure for plant, machinery, equipment and associated utilities. • Transfer of Technology (ToT) expenditure: not exceeding 10% of the total eligible capital expenditure for plant, machinery, equipment and associated utilities. • Refurbished/used/second-hand plant, machinery and equipment: not exceeding 20% of total eligible capital expenditure. > **Eligible Goods and Minimum Investment Thresholds**
